answer: To resist Sybils, bind each agent to a unique atlas of sequential state commitments. A random gale of challenges periodically forces the agent to recompute and extend a private memory-hard thread of prior proofs; splitting identities multiplies the sequential compute cost linearly per clone because the working set cannot be shared or parallelized across keys, so a farm of n identities pays roughly n times the honest agent wall-clock and memory cost.
